title: What is a Fortune?
paragraphs: The evening of life portrayed by Tolkāppiyar

Could be compared with the perennial river merging into the sea Originating from the hills and flowing through the paddy fields, It renders benefits a thousand before reaching the sea. Since it writes its epilogue while merging into the sea, Nobody would conclude that the story of the river is all at a close. Even the lives of the dead continue through their progeny. The same is applicable to the river.
Continuing to live even after death is an honour to great people.
The sun is warm at rise and goes scorching at the peak, And before vanishing in the west, Thanks to the comforting south wind, Showers happiness upon the entire earth.
Likewise, The aged who are in the last phase of their life, Having enjoyed the felicities of conjugal life
And having reaped all that it offered, Will have their fortune realized As they live surrounded by pleasant children And comfort-giving kindred folks And live in serenity Taking to ways of virtue.

> Having relished the felicities of the passion of love, > It is for the hero and heroine in conjugal union > To savour the protective presence of their children > And seek to live on things sublime, > With virtuous kinsfolk around, > Which makes for the fruits the wedded course entailed.
